chapter_title: The Human is less than all the Things of the Unive
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation of the K
ephalaia
 Passage


---


**
¶2.
** After the Divine had taken
 its
 stand in the very
 midst of the infl
owing truth, it
 disclosed
 from
 its governing
 wisdom what
 follows
:
 If
 all
 the
 sens
ory cognitions belonging
 to the proprium —
 however
 many could
 be gathered
 from
 the ou
termost plane of the natural mind,
 even
 those
 drawn
 up
 from what
 is interior
 — were
 assembled
 and
 set
 in order one
 beside
 another across
 the whole
 extent
 of the natural
 understanding
, they
 could not,
 even
 taken
 together, rise
 to the elevated
 state of celestial perception. They
 could not attain the fullness of
 that
 perception
 in
 the
 bread
th of its
 wisdom
, nor in the width of its truth
, nor in the depth of its interior
 good
.
 No
 arrangement
 of merely
 natural knowing
 can
 equal
 the dimensions
 of what
 is perceived
 from
 an
 elevated spiritual
 state.

---


**¶3.**
 Nor
 is
 this
 all
.
 Every
 one of these
 natural
 cogn
itions, from
 the
 least
 to the greatest, is as
 if
 cast
 into the
 vast
 gathering of knowledges in
 the general
 memory
,
 and there
 they are sw
allowed up and lost
. Within
 the natural
 mind there
 are
 many
 elevated
 per
ceptions
, and
 the
 encomp
assing field
 of knowledge
 is very
 great
 in
 its own
 manner
 —
 yet
 these
 elevated
 perceptions offered
 no resistance to the Divine.
 They remained
 in a state
 of receptive
 still
ness.
 They did
 not deny
 or profane His
 manifest
 wisdom
, nor did they 
utter fals
ities against the
 Divine omn
ipotence that sustains all states
 of
 existence
,
 nor against the Divine
 being
 itself
 that
 is
 made
 known throughout
 every
 plane
,
 nor against the good works that
 proceed
 from Divine
 order. They attributed
 no origin of evil to God
.


---

**¶4.
** However, the false
 self-derived image that
 fallen
 humanity fash
ions — an
 image
 unlike
 any
 true
 conception,
 which
 sets
 itself as
 equal
 to the Divine and
 to
 His
 great
 works — was
 found
 to be evil before
 the
 Lord
 of
 all. This
 false image
 of
 the prop
rium denied
 the very
 omn
ipotence that sustains all existence
. It prof
aned the glory
 of Divine
 wisdom and
 became
 the origin
 of every transg
ression. For
 those
 who reason
 from
 this
 false image
 declare
 that every
 v
ile evil
 and imp
urity, every
 evil
 aff
ection and false persuasion, every
 inf
ernal love and destruct
ive impul
se,
 has
 come
 forth
 from God
 Himself —
 that He
 is the one
 who established them.
 Yet
 these
 things
 did
 not proceed
 from Him
.
 Those
 who assert
 this bear
 false
 witness against the Divine
.

---

**¶7
.** The
 Divine Truth
 did
 not desc
end and
 accomplish
 redemption for the sake
 of the human
 mind
 alone. It
 came and made
 itself manifest
 upon
 the
 natural
 plane, and its
 power
 operated
 throughout
 the
 universal
 spiritual world. And
 when it had completed
 its work throughout
 every
 external
 state
 in
 the grand
 order
 of creation
, it descended
 further
 into the most
 ancient
 celestial states
 —
 the earliest
 perceptive humanity
 —
 and revealed itself to them
. Even so, it sent forth
 essential
 truths into
 every
 good
 state
, from
 one
 successive
 dispens
ation of
 the church to the next,
 and through
 them
 revealed five
 fundamental
 spiritual
 knowledges.

---

**
¶9.** Second
: It unveiled to them the
 nature
 of the
 eternal
 states
 proce
eding from the Divine —
 how they come
 into
 being.
 And
 it taught them concerning
 the nature of falsity from
 evil —
 how it,
 too, has
 its manner
 of subsistence.

---

**
¶10.** Third: It
 proclaimed to them how
 the full
ness of Divine
 wisdom
 has
 acted
 against the dominion of falsity,
 and has
 prev
ailed over
 it.

---

**¶
11.** Fourth: It taught them
 that the Divine descended
 into the
 very
 state
 of spiritual death —
 into
 what
 belongs
 to the prop
rium —
 until it should recover
 what is its
 own and
 bring souls
 forth
 from the entrance
 to
 the inf
ernal states below
,
 for they had been wholly
 overwhel
med and
 consumed
 by those
 states
.

---

**¶13
.** All the faithful who receive
 this truth
 into
 their life
 shall live by three great essential
 powers
 —
 which
 are love to
 the Lord, wisdom from
 Him
, and a
 life
 of use according
 to both
.
